name: Travel Planner by Gildhart
changelog:
• Reminders. A visitor who gives a flight date more than eight weeks away is offered a reminder for the day eight weeks before they fly, when it is time to book a travel consultation: as a calendar file or a Google Calendar link, which keep nothing about them (the site counts how many were added each month, and that is all). The card gives the NHS's advice on when to be seen.
  • Reminders by email, off until the pharmacy ticks them in Travel Planner > Settings > Reminders, where the line for the site's privacy notice is. The visitor gives an address and ticks their agreement; they are emailed once to confirm, with a link that cancels it, and once on the day; the address and the trip are then deleted. WordPress's own Export and Erase Personal Data tools find and delete a person's reminder. Travel Planner > Look-ups shows how many, never who.
  • Posts to share. For each outbreak notice of the last 30 days about a disease the pharmacy vaccinates against, Travel Planner > Posts to share drafts a Google Business Profile post, a short social post and an email: the notice's day, disease and country, and the travel consultation. The most worth sharing come first: a country the site has a guide for, then the countries its visitors look up most. Nothing is posted or sent: a person reads, copies and shares it, and marks it as shared. The notice email says when a draft is ready.
  • A reminder and a post say "travel consultation" and never name a vaccine, a dose or a price: both are advertisements, and UK advertising rules (CAP Code 12.12) do not allow a prescription-only medicine to be advertised to the public. The vaccines and prices stay on the site's own pages, which they link to.
  • Settings: reminders (on) and remind_email (off), on the screen and in a site's file.
